n:Accountant General of Barbados: The Accountant General of Barbados, in Bridgetown, keeps the government's books, and auditors have compared them with the Central Bank of Barbados. The 2004 Auditor General's report found that between October 2000 and February 2004 the two sets of records for the government current account did not match, with unrecorded withdrawals above $1.8 million and unrecorded deposits above $6.8 million, including a $4.48 million transaction flagged in 2003. The 2020 report found eight loan-fund transfers totalling $13.137 million made without the signed memorandum the Accountant General gives the bank.
n:Algemene Rekenkamer Aruba: Aruba's General Audit Chamber in Oranjestad checks how the country accounts for its money. Reviewing the annual accounts for 2001 to 2004, it found that money paid into an earmarked account held in Aruba's name at the Centrale Bank van Aruba for the Fondo Desaroyo Aruba foundation was not accounted for completely, correctly and on time. Of a balance of 19.3 million Aruban florins at the end of 2000, only the 3 million paid in by Aruba appeared; 16,898,503 florins paid in by the Netherlands were left off.
n:Barbados Audit Office: The Barbados Audit Office in Bridgetown audits government accounts, several of which sit at the Central Bank of Barbados. Its 2004 report found records of the government current account not matching the bank's between October 2000 and February 2004. The 2020 report found Treasury accounts unreconciled since May 2018, eight loan-fund transfers totalling $13.137 million without the required memorandum, and the government overdraft twice passing its statutory limit of 10 per cent of estimated revenue, $323.303 million. The 2021 report found an unexplained $6,662,541.31 cheque difference for 22 September 2020.
n:Cabinet of Malta: Malta's Cabinet, the country's government ministers in Valletta, was reported to have settled how the governorship of the Central Bank of Malta would be handled while its governor faced criminal charges. Edward Scicluna stepped aside from his functions as governor, with deputy governor Alexander Demarco replacing him. Scicluna had insisted he would not resign, and a Tuesday cabinet meeting appeared to have reached a compromise with him. Prime Minister Robert Abela insisted on the presumption of innocence; the charges are unproven. Scicluna keeps his salary, put at 138,000 euros.
n:Cabinet of Solomon Islands: The Cabinet in Honiara is the government of the Solomon Islands and has a standing role at the Central Bank of Solomon Islands. Under the Central Bank of Solomon Islands Act 2012, section 41(1) has the Governor-General appoint the Governor on Cabinet's recommendation and section 41(3) has the Minister for Finance appoint the other directors. Section 37 lets the Minister, with Cabinet's approval, give written directions, which must be published in the Gazette and laid before Parliament. Section 44 allows early removal only for permanent incapacity or serious misconduct.
n:Cabinet of Tonga: Tonga's Cabinet, the government in Nukuʻalofa, holds the appointments at the National Reserve Bank of Tonga. Under the National Reserve Bank of Tonga Act, Chapter 16.12, 2020 Revised Edition, section 10(1) has the Minister, with Cabinet's consent, appoint five directors and name the Chairman and Deputy Chairman, and section 11(1) has Cabinet appoint the Governor. Section 50(1) allows written directives, and under section 50(4) a policy disagreement goes to Cabinet to decide. Section 11(3) permits the Governor's removal only for incapacity, serious misconduct or failure to perform his duties.
n:Cabinet of the Cayman Islands: The Cabinet of the Cayman Islands, the government in George Town, sits over the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority. Under the Monetary Authority Law (2020 Revision), revised as at 31 December 2019 and still the main Act after a 2024 amendment touched only fees and regulation-making, section 12(1) has the Cabinet appoint the directors, section 11(3) designate the chairperson and deputy, and section 13(1) appoint the managing director. Section 33(1) lets it give written general directions in the public interest, which the Authority must follow.
n:Commission of inquiry of the Assembly: A commission of inquiry of the Comoros Assembly in Moroni examined the economic citizenship programme, which sold passports. Reporting in December 2017, it said that according to his own collaborators President Ikililou Dhoinine ordered that from January 2015 the money no longer be paid into the Banque Centrale des Comores and could not explain what became of it; it concluded he was suspected of embezzling public money, which is unproven. It also found the programme account TR0044 took in money without the bank knowing what passports sold for.
n:Comoro Gulf Holding: Comoro Gulf Holding is a company in Moroni, Comoros, named in a parliamentary inquiry's account of money held at the Banque Centrale des Comores. The inquiry recorded that the economic citizenship account TR0044 at the central bank received payments including four cheques drawn by Comoro Gulf Holding on two commercial banks between March 2009 and April 2010, and that the bank booked money into the account without knowing the price at which the passports were being sold. The account was closed on 1 September 2015.
n:Council of Ministers of Syria: The Council of Ministers in Damascus is Syria's cabinet, and the law places the Central Bank of Syria under it. Basic Monetary Law No. 23 of 2002, issued on 17 March 2002 by President Bashar al-Assad, says the Monetary and Credit Council, which sets monetary policy, works within the state's general economic directions as approved by the Council of Ministers. Under article 8(3) the Minister of Economy and Foreign Trade may suspend a Council decision for up to seven days and refer a continuing disagreement to the Council of Ministers.
n:Câmara de Contas of Timor-Leste: The Câmara de Contas in Dili is Timor-Leste's Court of Accounts, which audits state accounts. In its report on the 2019 General State Account it found that 6.6 million US dollars of European Union budget support, held in three accounts at the Banco Central de Timor-Leste, had not been booked as state revenue, so 2019 revenue was understated by that amount, and the 2.3 million US dollars spent from those accounts went outside the state budget.
n:Government of Fiji: The Government of Fiji, based in Suva, removed the governor of the Reserve Bank of Fiji. Officials took Savenaca Narube out of the post and put deputy governor Sada Reddy in his place, hours before the Fiji dollar was devalued by 20 per cent. The government had come to power the previous week and was led by the army. No official reason was given for the removal; Narube had recently warned about the economy and forecast a 0.3 per cent contraction for 2009.
n:Governor of Aruba: The Governor of Aruba, based in Oranjestad, holds the appointments at the Centrale Bank van Aruba. Under Aruba's Central Bank Ordinance (AB 1991 no. GT 32), as amended through AB 2014 no. 5, section 18 has the Governor appoint the president and executive directors from a shortlist of three put up by the Supervisory Board, and allows dismissal by state decree. Section 23 has the Governor appoint and dismiss the Government Commissioner, who chairs that board and supervises the bank on the Minister's instructions.
